article_title: Neonatal Training across Union of European Medical Specialists Member Countries: A Survey from the Next Generation of Neonatologists.
citation: Williams Emma, Dassios Theodore, Alonso-Ojembarrena Almudena, Roehr Charles C., Been Jasper V., Pieter de Boode Willem, Jost Kerstin. (2025). Neonatal Training across Union of European Medical Specialists Member Countries: A Survey from the Next Generation of Neonatologists. Neonatology. https://doi.org/10.1159/000547673
title: Structured online survey of neonatal trainees across UEMS member countries on pulmonology training
description: A structured online questionnaire distributed via the ESPR newsletter and targeted national neonatology societies from 35 full and associate member countries of the UEMS between December 2023 and June 2024. It collected demographic information, training description, research activity, and self-rated confidence (1–5) and supervision-requirement levels for manual tasks and clinical decision-making, plus readiness to become a consultant on a 1–10 scale. One hundred and eight individual responses from 24 countries were received; 105 were analysed.
requirements: Distribution via ESPR newsletter and national neonatology societies
Eligibility restricted to current NST or those who completed training within the last 3 years
constraints: Risk of selection bias as the survey was not mandatory
Distribution through the ESPR introduced bias toward trainees from more academically inclined institutions
target_learners: Junior consultants who completed training within the last 3 years
target_learning_goals: Assessment of training experiences and confidence in pulmonology-related skills
key_sources: Williams Emma, Dassios Theodore, Alonso-Ojembarrena Almudena, Roehr Charles C., Been Jasper V., Pieter de Boode Willem, Jost Kerstin. (2025). Neonatal Training across Union of European Medical Specialists Member Countries: A Survey from the Next Generation of Neonatologists. Neonatology. https://doi.org/10.1159/000547673

article_title: Gamified Automation in Immersive Media for Education and Research
citation: Janelle Resch, Ireneusz (Eric) Ocelewski, Judy Ehrentraut, and Mike Barnett-Cowan. (2018). Gamified Automation in Immersive Media for Education and Research. https://arxiv.org/abs/1901.00729v1
title: Unreal Engine 4 blueprints visual scripting system
description: UE4 is a video game developer platform from Epic Games for building VR and AR experiences, written mostly in C++. Its blueprints system is a node-based visual scripting interface in the Unreal Editor where "different color nodes are used to define an event, or function, or variable" connected by colored wires, and a blueprint is equivalent to an object-oriented class in C++. UE4 converts blueprints into C++, and the article states "Using blueprints is especially useful for quick prototyping of an idea". The paper positions blueprints as lowering the barrier for non-specialists entering development.
requirements: Requires the Unreal Editor development environment; projects using blueprints are converted by UE4 into C++.
target_learners: general public new to software development
target_learning_goals: rapid prototyping of interactive VR/AR learning and research tools
examples: The paper's case studies used UE4 with NVIDIA libraries to build a VR brass-acoustics visualization and HoloLens kinesiology demonstrations.
key_sources: Janelle Resch, Ireneusz (Eric) Ocelewski, Judy Ehrentraut, and Mike Barnett-Cowan. (2018). Gamified Automation in Immersive Media for Education and Research. https://arxiv.org/abs/1901.00729
